The axis roles of an anipoint, and the columns carrying them

Source: R/axes.R
get_axes.Rd

The where$position slot. Index by role to write a transformation that does not care what the columns are called: data[[get_axes(data)[["x"]]]].

Usage

get_axes(data)

Arguments

data

An anipoint object.

Value

Named character vector: names are axis roles (x, y, z, rho, phi, theta), values are the columns carrying them. Empty for a frame whose coordinate system is "unknown".

See also

set_variables() to change it.

Examples

af <- example_anipoint(n_obs = 3, n_individuals = 1, n_keypoints = 1)
get_axes(af)
#>   x   y 
#> "x" "y" 

df <- data.frame(time = 1:3, individual = "a", u = c(1, 2, 3), v = c(0, 1, 0))
renamed <- as_anipoint(df, variables_where = c(x = "u", y = "v"))
get_axes(renamed)
#>   x   y 
#> "u" "v" 
get_metadata(renamed, "coordinate_system")
#> [1] cartesian_2d
#> 7 Levels: unknown cartesian_1d cartesian_2d cartesian_3d polar ... spherical
